standard_prerequisites.name: The cap with the class of a relative effective Cartier divisor as a left inverse of the pushforward along the projection

standard_prerequisites.use: Since $o(X)$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $L$, it gives $o^* \circ p^* = \text{id}$, which forces injectivity of $p^*$.

core_obligations: Obtain surjectivity of $p^*$ from the affine fibres lemma (proof line 5753).

Introduce the zero section $o$, identify it with the morphism belonging to the surjection $\text{Sym}^*(\mathcal{L}) \to \mathcal{O}_X$, and record $p \circ o = \text{id}_X$ and that $o(X)$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $L$ (proof lines 5754-5757).
Apply the relative effective Cartier divisor lemma to get $o^* \circ p^* = \text{id}$, hence injectivity, and combine with surjectivity (proof lines 5758-5760).
proof_roadmap: Surjectivity from the affine fibre lemma (proof line 5753).
The zero section and its divisor property (proof lines 5754-5757).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the flat pullback along the total space of the vector bundle attached to an invertible sheaf is an isomorphism on Chow groups, shifting degrees by one (statement lines 5736-5750). The proof obtains surjectivity from the general affine fibre result and injectivity by exhibiting the zero section, whose image is an effective Cartier divisor, as a left inverse up to the cap with that divisor. The construction of the left inverse is the substance, so the claim is H2.
